title: clipboard-history: ships dev.enable+source+autoStart, prelude fetched from 127.0.0.1:3488
summary: The shipped official manifest commits a dev-mode block with enable/source true and a localhost dev address. plugin.ts loadPreludeScript() takes the remote branch whenever dev.enable && dev.source && dev.address, so the plugin's Prelude is fetched over HTTP from 127.0.0.1:3488 instead of the packaged file.
failure_scenario: End user installs the packaged app; clipboard-history loads with dev.enable=true so the runtime issues GET http://127.0.0.1:3488/index.js. Nothing listens on that port, the request fails and the plugin never loads. If any unrelated local process does listen on 3488, whatever body it returns is executed as the plugin Prelude. plugin-loaders.ts:249-255 only coerces the values (enable: rawDevConfig.enable === true) and there is no app.isPackaged guard anywhere on this path.
recommendation: Set dev.enable to false in the committed manifest and gate the remote-prelude branch on !app.isPackaged.

title: touch-intelligence: ships dev.enable+source, prelude fetched from 127.0.0.1:5174
summary: The AI plugin's committed manifest enables dev mode with source:true and a localhost address, so its 3000-line Prelude is loaded over the network from a dev server rather than from disk.
failure_scenario: In a packaged build the runtime resolves new URL('index.js', 'http://127.0.0.1:5174/') and GETs it with a 5s timeout (plugin.ts:1993-2007). On a user machine the fetch fails and the AI plugin - which owns intelligence.basic and the ai/@ai CoreBox prefix - silently fails to load; the local index.js sitting next to the manifest is never used.
recommendation: Set dev.enable to false before release and add a packaged-build guard.

title: touch-translation: ships dev.enable+source, prelude fetched from localhost:3733
summary: Committed manifest enables dev mode with source:true pointing at a localhost Vite address, diverting Prelude loading to the network in shipped builds.
failure_scenario: Packaged app loads touch-translation, hits the dev branch in plugin.ts:1992, GETs http://localhost:3733/index.js, times out after 5s and the translation plugin (network.internet + intelligence.basic + storage.plugin) fails to initialize. The bundled index.js is bypassed.
recommendation: Flip dev.enable to false in the committed manifest.

title: plugins:validate has no dev.enable check, so committed dev leakage passes the gate
summary: AGENTS.md prescribes `pnpm plugins:validate` as the manifest gate, but the validator never inspects the dev block. Running it against the current tree reports 24/24 passed while three manifests ship dev.enable:true with localhost addresses.
evidence:
Actual run output: `24/24 plugins passed validation.` / `All plugins validated successfully.` A grep for dev handling in the script returns only line 126-127, which is about a missing manifest, not the dev block:
  logWarn(pluginName, hasPackageJson ? 'manifest.json not found — skipping Surface-only plugin' : 'manifest.json not found — skipping')
failure_scenario: A contributor follows plugins/AGENTS.md:52 ('Manifest 校验：pnpm plugins:validate'), sees an all-green result, and ships clipboard-history / touch-intelligence / touch-translation with dev.enable:true. The prescribed gate cannot catch the exact class of defect it is cited for.
recommendation: Fail validation when a committed manifest has dev.enable true.

title: touch-image: no manifest.json in the repo, plugin cannot be loaded at all
summary: touch-image tracks no manifest.json. Its only manifest is dist/manifest.json, an untracked build artifact in the pre-SDK legacy schema with no id, no sdkapi, no permissions and no features.
failure_scenario: The loader only ever reads manifest.json (plugin-loaders.ts / official-plugin-seed.ts:75). With none present the plugin is skipped entirely — `node scripts/validate-plugins.mjs` prints `[touch-image] manifest.json not found — skipping Surface-only plugin`. Even if dist/manifest.json were used, checkSdkCompatibility blocks it: missing sdkapi returns compatible:false ('must declare sdkapi >= 251212').
recommendation: Add a real manifest.json in the current schema or remove the plugin from the workspace.

title: touch-music: no manifest.json, only a legacy init.json nothing reads
summary: touch-music ships init.json, a pre-manifest config format. No code in apps/ or packages/ reads init.json, and the plugin has no manifest.json, so it can never load.
failure_scenario: validate-plugins.mjs reports `[touch-music] manifest.json not found — skipping Surface-only plugin`. The plugin is dead weight in the workspace: it is built and linted by CI but the runtime can never register it, and the stale init.json misleads contributors into thinking it is configured.
recommendation: Either port touch-music to a current manifest.json or delete it along with init.json.

title: touch-image: package.json embeds talex-touch.plugin.dev.enable:true with 127.0.0.1:6001
summary: The committed package.json carries a talex-touch block that turns on dev mode and hardcodes a localhost address; this block is what the build copies into dist/manifest.json.
failure_scenario: Anyone building touch-image gets dist/manifest.json with dev.enable:true baked in, reproducing the same localhost-dev leakage as the three shipped manifests, and there is no validator step that inspects package.json talex-touch blocks.
recommendation: Set enable to false, or move the dev address into a git-ignored local override.

title: touch-music: five declared dependencies are never imported (xterm, wavesurfer, granim, milkdown)
summary: package.json declares xterm, xterm-addon-fit, wavesurfer.js, granim and @milkdown/theme-nord, none of which appear anywhere in src/, vite.config.js or index.html.
evidence:
plugins/touch-music/package.json dependencies include:
    "@milkdown/theme-nord": "^7.21.2",
    "granim": "^2.0.0",
    "wavesurfer.js": "^7.12.10",
    "xterm": "^5.3.0",
    "xterm-addon-fit": "^0.8.0"
Grepping each name across plugins/touch-music/src, vite.config.js and index.html returns 0 matches (only rgbaster, which is used, returns 1).
failure_scenario: pnpm install pulls a terminal emulator, a waveform renderer, a gradient library and a markdown editor theme into an example music plugin, inflating the workspace lockfile and install time with packages no code path can reach.
recommendation: Drop the unused dependencies from package.json.

title: touch-quick-actions: executes lock-screen/mute/shutdown inside onFeatureTriggered, the display callback
summary: The dynamic quick-action-* features run system.runAction directly from onFeatureTriggered instead of publishing an item and executing in onItemAction. onFeatureTriggered is re-entered on every input change while the feature is active, so the mutating system action fires repeatedly.
failure_scenario: apps/core-app/src/main/modules/plugin/adapters/plugin-features-adapter.ts:160-161 calls BOTH `await plugin.triggerFeature(feature, query)` and `await plugin.triggerInputChanged(feature, query)` on each input change, and both invoke onFeatureTriggered (plugin.ts:1008 and plugin.ts:1044). For lock-screen and mute-toggle the host requires no confirmation (plugin-system-capabilities.ts:40-41 `'lock-screen': {risk:'immediate', confirmation:'none'}`), so activating the feature locks the screen and every following keystroke locks it again. For shutdown/restart (confirmation:'double') the destructive confirmation dialog is re-raised on each keystroke. touch-system-actions uses the same system.runAction capability but correctly defers it to onItemAction.
recommendation: Publish an item from onFeatureTriggered and move runAction into onItemAction, as touch-system-actions does.

title: touch-quick-actions: onFeatureTriggered returns an action-result object, breaking the boolean|void contract
summary: onFeatureTriggered returns the object produced by runAction/blocked ({externalAction, success, status, reason, message}) but the lifecycle contract is boolean | void, where false means 'do not enter activation state'.
failure_scenario: plugin-features-adapter.ts:376 checks `typeof shouldActivate === 'boolean' && shouldActivate === false`. A returned object is never boolean, so even when runAction returns {status:'blocked', reason:'confirmation-denied'} the provider stays activated and CoreBox keeps the feature open with no items pushed - the user sees an empty active feature after declining a shutdown confirmation. plugins/touch-quick-actions/index.test.cjs:167-173 asserts on result.status/result.reason, codifying the wrong contract.
recommendation: Return true/false from onFeatureTriggered and surface action results through onItemAction.

title: touch-workspace-scripts: onFeatureTriggered throws to the host, tripping the auto-disable circuit breaker
summary: When the workspaceScripts capability is missing, onFeatureTriggered throws instead of publishing a degraded item. The throw is outside the try/catch that begins on the next line, so it escapes into the plugin host on every invocation.
failure_scenario: Every throw routes to plugin.ts:1022 `await this.handleRuntimeError('onFeatureTriggered', error)`, which pushes an issue and appends to a 60s sliding error window. plugin.ts:1376-1388: `if (this._runtimeStats.errorTimestamps.length > 10) { ... this.status = PluginStatus.CRASHED; await this.disable() }`. Because onFeatureTriggered fires on each input change (plugin.ts:1044), a user typing 'workspace scripts' with the capability unavailable produces >10 errors within seconds and the plugin is marked CRASHED and disabled, requiring manual re-enable.
recommendation: Publish the 'workspace scripts unavailable' info item instead of throwing, matching onItemAction.

title: All plugin manifests declare feature.platform in a shape IPlatform does not define, and it is never enforced
summary: Every manifest writes platform as {win32: boolean, darwin: boolean, linux: boolean}, but the IPlatform type is keyed win|darwin|linux with IPlatformInfo objects. The runtime never evaluates manifest feature.platform at all, so platform restrictions are silently inert.
evidence:
plugins/touch-window-presets/manifest.json:52-56 declares Windows-only support:
      "platform": {
        "win32": true,
        "darwin": false,
        "linux": false
      },

The type, packages/utils/plugin/index.ts:73-77:
  export type PlatformKey = 'win' | 'darwin' | 'linux'
  export type IPlatform = { [key in PlatformKey]?: IPlatformInfo }
with IPlatformInfo = { enable: boolean; arch: Arch[]; os: SupportOS[] } (line 67-71).

The host's own validator for runtime-registered features requires that shape: plugin-business-capabilities.ts:1052-1057 `exactRecord(requiredField(record, 'platform'), ['win', 'darwin', 'linux'])` then `exactRecord(platformRecord[key], ['enable', 'arch', 'os'])`.
failure_scenario: Grepping feature.platform across the main process finds only pass-through assignments (plugin.ts:803 and plugin.ts:1469); no code reads .win32, .win or .enable to filter features. touch-window-presets, touch-quick-actions, touch-system-actions, touch-window-manager and touch-browser-open all declare linux:false but their features still register and surface in CoreBox on Linux. They only avoid broken behaviour because each prelude re-checks the platform itself (e.g. touch-window-presets/index.js:192 `if (currentPlatform() !== 'win32')`); a plugin that trusts the manifest declaration gets no gating. Note touch-browser-open/index.js:125-133 builds the correct {win:{enable,arch,os}} shape for runtime-registered features, so the two shapes disagree inside one plugin.
recommendation: Pick one shape, enforce it in validate-plugins.mjs, and gate feature registration on it.

title: touch-batch-rename: missing permission SDK is reported as permission-denied, hiding the real reason
summary: hasPermission collapses 'permission SDK absent' and 'check threw' into the same false as 'permission genuinely denied', so both apply and undo report reason 'permission-denied'.
failure_scenario: If the permission facade is not injected (capability gated off) the user sees '缺少 fs.write 权限' and is told to grant a permission they may already hold, with no path to diagnose the real fault. plugins/AGENTS.md:27 requires the opposite: '返回结果保留具体 reason：permission-denied、permission-sdk-unavailable、permission-request-failed 等'.
recommendation: Return a discriminated result from hasPermission and map it to permission-sdk-unavailable / permission-request-failed / permission-denied.

title: touch-dictation: bare catch blocks discard every failure reason and plugin.voice is dereferenced unguarded
summary: The optional-chaining guard tests plugin.voice?.asrStream but the fallback calls plugin.voice.dictate without a guard, and the surrounding catch blocks take no error binding, so permission-denied, sdk-unavailable and transport failures all collapse into one generic message with no reason field.
failure_scenario: When the voice capability is not injected at all, plugin.voice is undefined; the guard on line 90 is satisfied (undefined !== 'function') and line 91 throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'dictate'). The bare catch swallows it and tells the user to check microphone permissions, which is unrelated to the actual fault. Unlike every sibling plugin, the returned object carries no `reason` or `status`, violating plugins/AGENTS.md:27 ('返回结果保留具体 reason'). onSpeakAction at line 157-168 has the identical pattern for plugin.voice.speak.
recommendation: Guard plugin.voice before use and bind the error to map PLUGIN_HOST_CAPABILITY_* codes to explicit reasons, as touch-snipaste's stableFailure does.

title: touch-browser-open: onInputChanged handler is dead code - the host never invokes the prelude hook
summary: The plugin implements onInputChanged to refresh search suggestions, but nothing in the main process ever calls the prelude's onInputChanged. It is declared on the lifecycle proxy and the wire allowlist yet has no call site.
failure_scenario: The handler and the activeSearch state it maintains never run. Suggestions still refresh only because plugin-features-adapter.ts:160-161 re-invokes onFeatureTriggered, so the dead path silently duplicates working logic. The `signal` parameter is also unreachable: the proxy forwards a single argument, so any plugin adopting the documented hook (packages/utils/plugin/index.ts:386) gets a handler that is never called.
recommendation: Either wire the lifecycle hook in the main process or drop it from the SDK surface and from this plugin.
